scope: Native range-read drive ownership; fragmented FAT bytes, nested callers, read failures and cleanup. No whole-IWAD buffering or filesystem implementation change.

results.out: WAD LOCK 26 CASES 16 FAULTS 7 GAPS BAD 0

cases: Eight-cluster file constructed by alternating allocations with another file; seven nonadjacent links are required and observed.
Whole-file, cached first-cluster, aligned bulk and unaligned reads compare every returned byte and both destination guards.
Both previously unlocked and caller-owned drive/device states are preserved.
All four FBlkRead call sites fail once by returning FALSE and once by throwing, under both ownership states; no task heap leak.
Negative, past-end and empty ranges are checked without disk access.
526 actual Freedoom ranges, read three times each, match independent host hashes (1,578 native reads).
limits: The block and drive unlock routines retain their native yields. The application holds the drive for one requested range, not across rendering or the complete level load.
No throughput or universal host-performance claim; actual-window transition qualification is recorded separately.
The native fixture uses FAT32; existing contiguous/RedSea FBlkRead behavior is retained but not newly qualified by this fixture.
